frozen_decisions_applied: S6's own required-changes text, verbatim: 'Before implementing the control-plane changes, create the Kconfig definitions and one typed security-bounds accessor consumed by provisioning, Web parsing, rate limiting and audit storage.' -- implemented as exactly this: ten new Kconfig symbols plus one C++ accessor, consumed by nothing yet (each of the four named future consumers is its own later sub-slice).

Plan text: 'The typed accessor is the only application-facing source for tunables; handlers/adapters must not repeat numeric literals.' -- security_bounds() is designed as the single point every future S6 component will read from; this sub-slice does not yet have any such component to enforce this against, but the accessor itself is built to be that single source.

Plan text: 'The provisioning passphrase length remains a non-configurable 16 Base32 characters, and login backoff remains a non-configurable 2-second start with a 60-second maximum.' -- implemented as fixed constexpr members, not Kconfig symbols, so no build configuration can set them differently.

Plan text: 'An in-range change from the approved default requires a reviewed release-manifest delta... rather than an automatic rejection solely for differing from the default.' -- verify_tunable_ranges() checks range membership only, never equality to the default; verified directly by a dedicated test (test_in_range_non_default_value_passes).

kconfig_symbols_added.detail: 10 new int Kconfig symbols in a new 'Security' submenu of main/Kconfig.projbuild, each with a real `range MIN MAX` (matching this repository's own existing precedent, e.g. ZGW_OTA_BOOT_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_MS) and the plan's exact approved default. Verified against a real idf.py build that all 10 appear in the generated sdkconfig with the expected default values.

typed_accessor_implemented.detail: security_bounds.hpp/.cpp: SecurityBounds struct (10 configurable fields + 3 fixed constexpr non-configurable constants), security_bounds() (ESP_PLATFORM reads real CONFIG_ZGW_* macros once into a static instance; host builds fall back to the same approved-default values, letting every later host-tested S6 component build/test against real numbers without a real sdkconfig), security_bound_range()/security_bound_value_in_range() (the same range table exposed as a runtime-callable predicate, single-sourced with the host-fallback defaults within this file).

verifier_extended.detail: verify_production_security_profile.py's TUNABLE_RANGES + verify_tunable_ranges() reject an absent, unparseable, or out-of-range tunable, but explicitly allow an in-range non-default value (the plan's own carve-out). sdkconfig.production.esp32c6 pins all 10 tunables explicitly at their approved defaults, keeping RepositoryLayeredProfileTest's simulated-concatenation check passing and making the approved profile visible in one file rather than depending on an implicit Kconfig default.

real_kconfig_range_behavior_confirmed.detail: Edited a real generated sdkconfig to set CONFIG_ZGW_JSON_MAX_DEPTH=999 (its declared range is [2,4]) and ran idf.py reconfigure inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5: ESP-IDF's own Kconfig tooling printed a real warning ('user value 999 on the int symbol ZGW_JSON_MAX_DEPTH ... ignored due to being outside the active range ([2, 4]) -- falling back on defaults') and the regenerated sdkconfig reverted the value to 4, the approved default. This directly confirms the plan's own 'Kconfig rejects out-of-range values' text as real, observed ESP-IDF behavior.

tests_and_verification.detail: 8 new Python tests (VerifyTunableRangesTest, looping over TUNABLE_RANGES rather than hand-writing 10 separate cases): approved fixture passes; every tunable passes at its exact min/max; every tunable fails one-below-min/one-above-max; an in-range non-default value passes; a missing tunable fails; an unparseable value fails. 38/38 passing in scripts/test_verify_production_security_profile.py overall. 5 new C++ tests (test/host/test_security_bounds.cpp): host fallback matches approved defaults exactly; the 3 fixed constants have the plan's exact values; security_bounds() returns a stable reference; security_bound_range() matches the plan's table for all 10 fields (checked against the plan text directly, not tautologically against the function's own output); security_bound_value_in_range() checked at and around one boundary. Full repository host suite: 92/92 passing (91 pre-existing from S5 + this sub-slice's new executable). cppcheck: zero findings against security_bounds.cpp. check_arch_invariants.sh: high=0/medium=0/low=0, unchanged.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Only the 'Security invariants, bounded tunables and typed accessors' cluster is implemented; none of S6's numbered required changes #1-#37 (provisioning, HTTPS/sessions, authorization/physical presence, strict JSON parsing, rate limiting/audit, MQTT security) has started.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The plan's own text explicitly orders this cluster before all of them ('Before implementing the control-plane changes, create the Kconfig definitions and one typed security-bounds accessor'); the user's instruction was simply to move to S6, and this is the plan-mandated first piece, matching S5's own precedent of starting with its own foundational cluster (the production security profile) before anything else.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: Nothing in this repository calls security_bounds() yet -- it is fully implemented and tested scaffolding with zero real consumers, exactly matching every S5 sub-slice's own 'foundation only' pattern.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The (minimum, maximum, approved_default) table for the 10 tunables is declared independently, by hand, in three places: main/Kconfig.projbuild, security_bounds.cpp's kRanges, and verify_production_security_profile.py's TUNABLE_RANGES. Nothing automatically verifies the three stay in sync.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Kconfig, C++ and Python have no shared single-source-of-truth mechanism already established in this repository; generating one from another would be a larger, separate piece of tooling work not requested for this foundational sub-slice.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A future edit to one of the three tables without updating the other two would not be caught by any test in this repository today -- a real, named gap, not hidden.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: S6's plan-text precondition 'hardware security evidence... are available' is only partially satisfied -- the software-only half of S5 is complete (implementation-evidence/S5-completion.json), but real Secure Boot/Flash Encryption/NVS Encryption hardware readback remains BLOCKED_SECURITY_PROVISIONING. This sub-slice proceeded anyway, on the judgment that S6's Kconfig/accessor foundation work does not itself depend on that hardware evidence existing.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: This is a judgment call about what 'ready' means for a foundational, non-security-enforcing piece of scaffolding, not a resolution of the plan-text precondition itself -- deciding whether S6 as a WHOLE can proceed without real hardware evidence is a project-owner call this sub-slice does not make.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: If the project owner decides S6 cannot proceed at all without real hardware security evidence, this sub-slice's work is still valid (it does not depend on or claim any hardware property) but the decision to have started S6 at all would need revisiting.
